prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1032; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a sideswipe that occurred while the other vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through that office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. It places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the other driver's account, which matches the insured's description of the lane change.

Entry 3: Photographs from the scene and statements from two independent witnesses were collected. Both witnesses describe the same sequence of events, and the other driver has confirmed the account without qualification.

Entry 4: Damage to the claimant's vehicle was inspected. It is mostly confined to the side panels and mirror, which is consistent with the impact described, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 5: Claimant reported a back strain and began treatment through counsel's referral. The injury is consistent in type and force with a side impact of this kind, and no prior injury to the same area appears in our records.

Entry 6: A neighbor contacted the office saying the vehicle looked damaged a few weeks before the reported loss. This is a secondhand recollection with no supporting photos or records, and it has been noted for follow-up without changing the current assessment.

Entry 7: Each conversation with the claimant, including the recorded statement, has given the same account of the accident. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the medical file is being reviewed for the reasons.

Entry 8: The driver is confirmed as a named driver on the policy, and coverage applies. Remaining open items are the medical review and the neighbor's statement, and the file will be updated when counsel responds to the outstanding requests.
